The agent's response correctly identifies the instance (t3.micro burstable EBS performance) as the binding constraint, not the volume. It explicitly states the volume is over-provisioned ('volume size vs instance limit' section) noting the gp3 volume is provisioned at 16,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s while the instance can only drive ~11,800 IOPS at burst and 500 IOPS baseline - showing the volume has headroom relative to what the instance can deliver. It explicitly says 'The extra provisioned IOPS add cost without adding performance' and that right-sizing the volume down 'won't fix the slowness, since the instance is the bottleneck' - directly stating raising/changing volume IOPS will not help. It recommends an instance type change ('Move to a larger or non-burstable instance') as the primary fix. It never calls the volume saturated; instead it attributes the issue to EBSIOBalance% depletion at the instance level. This aligns well with the expected output: instance identified as binding layer, volume has headroom, volume IOPS change won't help, instance type change recommended, volume not called saturated.

One minor gap: the response doesn't explicitly mention reading from DescribeInstanceTypes API or explicitly summing IOPS across all attached volumes including root volume - but the substantive conclusion matches expectations. Given the instructions to focus on substance/meaning rather than exact mechanism citations, and that the core diagnostic conclusions align correctly, this should pass.
